Read the security review brief at /tmp/bench/notes/security-brief.md and follow it exactly. It also points to the audit findings table at /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md; read that too.

Your worktree: /tmp/bench/wt/sec2 (branch agent/sec2, based on commit ac6bde4). Run every cargo and git command with `cd /tmp/bench/wt/sec2` first.

Your scope (you may edit these files):
- contracts/src/proxy/** (IProxy, ERC-1967 and its utils, beacon proxy and upgradeable beacon, UUPS, ERC-1822)
- contracts/src/utils/storage_slot.rs and contracts/src/utils/address.rs (raw storage slots and the delegate-call helpers)
- contracts-proc/** (the openzeppelin-stylus-proc macros and interface_id)
- the framework-level unsafe surface: every `unsafe impl TopLevelStorage` in contracts/src (review soundness and whether any contract uses a component where the marker is unsound), and every `unsafe fn` (IProxy::delegate and do_fallback, StorageSlot raw access). You may change the code in your scope, but not the marker impls in files owned by other agents: report those instead.

Do NOT edit examples/, benches/, templates/, docs/, scripts/, .github/, any token/access/finance/utils file other than the two named above, lib/crypto/**, or any workspace manifest. Report requests instead.

Your notes file: /tmp/bench/notes/sec2-findings.md (write it as you go; the final report must match it).

Pay particular attention to: the UUPS upgrade path (who may upgrade, the implementation check, rollback to an implementation whose proxiableUUID is different, the ERC-1822 slot), the beacon (the implementation must have code, the upgrade must be authorised), ERC-1967 admin and implementation slots (writes must go through the checks), and delegate calls (the caller must control the target only where intended). Also check that the storage layout of every proxy-related struct is unchanged from v0.3.0 (compare the field order and types with `git show 47ad800:<file>`).

Commit each PoC test before its fix, as the brief requires. Use the Haiku trailer only.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

38	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain

43	    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).

48	    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
49	    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).

51	
52	## Test-harness facts you need
53	- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
54	  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
55	  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
56	  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
57	  before the call that needs it.

content.text: I'll start by reading the security brief and the audit findings table.

content.content:
1	# Security review brief (read fully before starting)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust), being migrated to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
4	1.91.0. The `bench` branch already contains the migrated contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
5	clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).
6	
7	Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
8	Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
9	`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
10	`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.
11	
12	## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
13	1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
14	2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
15	3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
16	4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
17	5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
18	   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
19	6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
20	   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
21	   are real issues in the code.
22	7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.
23	
24	## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
25	Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
26	you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
27	- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
28	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
29	- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
30	  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
31	  495-504).
32	- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
33	- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
34	  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
35	- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
36	  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
37	- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
38	  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
39	  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
40	- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
41	  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
42	  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
43	    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
44	  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
45	    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
46	    underlying token's).

54	  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
55	  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
56	  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
57	  before the call that needs it.
58	- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
59	  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.

64	## How to work
65	- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
66	  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
67	  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
68	  them in your notes file.
69	- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
70	  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
71	  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
72	  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
73	  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
74	- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
75	  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
76	  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
77	  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
78	- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
79	  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
80	- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the

67	    InvalidAdmin(ERC1967InvalidAdmin),
68	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `beacon`
69	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
70	    InvalidBeacon(ERC1967InvalidBeacon),
71	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that an upgrade function
72	    /// sees `self.vm().msg_value()` > [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]
73	    /// that may be lost.
74	    NonPayable(ERC1967NonPayable),
75	    /// There's no code at `target` (it is not a contract).
76	    EmptyCode(address::AddressEmptyCode),
77	    /// A call to an address target failed. The target may have reverted.
78	    FailedCall(address::FailedCall),
79	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the delegate call
80	    /// failed.
81	    FailedCallWithReason(address::FailedCallWithReason),
82	}

84	impl From<address::Error> for Error {
85	    fn from(e: address::Error) -> Self {
86	        match e {
87	            address::Error::EmptyCode(e) => Error::EmptyCode(e),
88	            address::Error::FailedCall(e) => Error::FailedCall(e),
89	            address::Error::FailedCallWithReason(e) => {
90	                Error::FailedCallWithReason(e)
91	            }
92	        }
93	    }
94	}

152	    /// Performs implementation upgrade with additional setup call if
153	    /// data is nonempty. This function is payable only if the setup call
154	    /// is performed, otherwise `context.vm().msg_value()` is rejected to avoid
155	    /// stuck value in the contract.
156	    ///
157	    /// # Arguments
158	    ///
159	    /// * `context` - Mutable access to the contract's state.
160	    /// * `new_implementation` - The new implementation address.
161	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the setup call.
162	    ///
163	    /// # Errors
164	    ///
165	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the `new_implementation` address
166	    ///   is not a valid implementation.
167	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If `data` is empty and
168	    ///   `context.vm().msg_value()` is not [`U256::ZERO`].
169	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the call to the implementation contract
170	    ///   fails.
171	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the call to the implementation
172	    ///   contract fails with a revert reason.
173	    pub fn upgrade_to_and_call<T: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>>(
174	        context: &mut T,
175	        new_implementation: Address,
176	        data: &Bytes,
177	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
178	        Erc1967Utils::set_implementation(context, new_implementation)?;
179	
180	        context
181	            .vm()
182	            .log(erc1967::Upgraded { implementation: new_implementation });
183	
184	        if data.is_empty() {
185	            Erc1967Utils::check_non_payable(context)?;
186	        } else {
187	            AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
188	                context,
189	                new_implementation,
190	                data.as_ref(),
191	            )?;
192	        }
193	
194	        Ok(())
195	    }

240	    /// Change the beacon and trigger a setup call if data is nonempty.
241	    /// This function is payable only if the setup call is performed,
242	    /// otherwise `context.vm().msg_value()` is rejected to avoid stuck value
243	    /// in the contract.
244	    ///
245	    /// # Arguments
246	    ///
247	    /// * `context` - Mutable access to the contract's state.
248	    /// * `new_beacon` - The new beacon address.

251	    /// # Errors
252	    ///
253	    /// * [`Error::InvalidBeacon`] - If the `new_beacon` address is not a valid
254	    ///   beacon.

258	    ///   `context.vm().msg_value()` is not [`U256::ZERO`].
259	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the call to the beacon implementation
260	    ///   fails.

262	    ///   implementation fails with a revert reason.
263	    pub fn upgrade_beacon_to_and_call<
264	        T: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>,
265	    >(
266	        context: &mut T,
267	        new_beacon: Address,
268	        data: &Bytes,
269	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
270	        Erc1967Utils::set_beacon(context, new_beacon)?;
271	        context.vm().log(erc1967::BeaconUpgraded { beacon: new_beacon });
272	
273	        if data.is_empty() {
274	            Erc1967Utils::check_non_payable(context)?;
275	        } else {
276	            let beacon_implementation =
277	                Erc1967Utils::get_beacon_implementation(context, new_beacon)?;
278	
279	            AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
280	                context,
281	                beacon_implementation,
282	                data.as_ref(),
283	            )?;
284	        }
285	
286	        Ok(())
287	    }

292	    /// [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]. It can be used to avoid
293	    /// `context.vm().msg_value()` stuck in the contract if an upgrade does not
294	    /// perform an initialization call.

296	    /// # Arguments
297	    ///

306	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
307	        if context.vm().msg_value().is_zero() {

309	        } else {

29	        /// * `implementation` - Address of the invalid implementation.

31	        #[allow(missing_docs)]

45	        /// * `beacon` - Address of the invalid `beacon` of the proxy.
46	        #[derive(Debug)]
47	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
48	        error ERC1967InvalidBeacon(address beacon);
49	
50	        /// Indicates an error related to the fact that an upgrade function
51	        /// sees `self.vm().msg_value()` > [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]

53	        #[derive(Debug)]
54	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
55	        error ERC1967NonPayable();

59	/// An [`Erc1967Utils`] error.
60	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
61	pub enum Error {
62	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `implementation`
63	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
64	    InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation),
65	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `admin` of the
66	    /// proxy is invalid.
67	    InvalidAdmin(ERC1967InvalidAdmin),
68	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `beacon`
69	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
70	    InvalidBeacon(ERC1967InvalidBeacon),
71	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that an upgrade function
72	    /// sees `self.vm().msg_value()` > [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]
73	    /// that may be lost.
74	    NonPayable(ERC1967NonPayable),
75	    /// There's no code at `target` (it is not a contract).
76	    EmptyCode(address::AddressEmptyCode),
77	    /// A call to an address target failed. The target may have reverted.
78	    FailedCall(address::FailedCall),
79	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the delegate call
80	    /// failed.
81	    FailedCallWithReason(address::FailedCallWithReason),

141	    /// Returns the current implementation address.
142	    ///
143	    /// # Arguments
144	    ///
145	    /// * `context` - Read access to the contract's state.

152	    /// Performs implementation upgrade with additional setup call if
153	    /// data is nonempty. This function is payable only if the setup call
154	    /// is performed, otherwise `context.vm().msg_value()` is rejected to avoid
155	    /// stuck value in the contract.
156	    ///
157	    /// # Arguments
158	    ///
159	    /// * `context` - Mutable access to the contract's state.
160	    /// * `new_implementation` - The new implementation address.
161	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the setup call.
162	    ///
163	    /// # Errors
164	    ///
165	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the `new_implementation` address
166	    ///   is not a valid implementation.
167	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If `data` is empty and
168	    ///   `context.vm().msg_value()` is not [`U256::ZERO`].
169	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the call to the implementation contract
170	    ///   fails.
171	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the call to the implementation
172	    ///   contract fails with a revert reason.
173	    pub fn upgrade_to_and_call<T: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>>(
174	        context: &mut T,
175	        new_implementation: Address,
176	        data: &Bytes,
177	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
178	        Erc1967Utils::set_implementation(context, new_implementation)?;
179	
180	        context
181	            .vm()
182	            .log(erc1967::Upgraded { implementation: new_implementation });
183	
184	        if data.is_empty() {
185	            Erc1967Utils::check_non_payable(context)?;
186	        } else {
187	            AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
188	                context,
189	                new_implementation,
190	                data.as_ref(),
191	            )?;
192	        }
193	
194	        Ok(())
195	    }

240	    /// Change the beacon and trigger a setup call if data is nonempty.
241	    /// This function is payable only if the setup call is performed,
242	    /// otherwise `context.vm().msg_value()` is rejected to avoid stuck value
243	    /// in the contract.
244	    ///
245	    /// # Arguments
246	    ///
247	    /// * `context` - Mutable access to the contract's state.
248	    /// * `new_beacon` - The new beacon address.
249	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the setup call.
250	    ///
251	    /// # Errors
252	    ///
253	    /// * [`Error::InvalidBeacon`] - If the `new_beacon` address is not a valid
254	    ///   beacon.
255	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the beacon implementation is not
256	    ///   a valid implementation.
257	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If `data` is empty and
258	    ///   `context.vm().msg_value()` is not [`U256::ZERO`].
259	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the call to the beacon implementation
260	    ///   fails.
261	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the call to the beacon
262	    ///   implementation fails with a revert reason.
263	    pub fn upgrade_beacon_to_and_call<
264	        T: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>,
265	    >(
266	        context: &mut T,
267	        new_beacon: Address,
268	        data: &Bytes,
269	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
270	        Erc1967Utils::set_beacon(context, new_beacon)?;
271	        context.vm().log(erc1967::BeaconUpgraded { beacon: new_beacon });
272	
273	        if data.is_empty() {
274	            Erc1967Utils::check_non_payable(context)?;
275	        } else {
276	            let beacon_implementation =
277	                Erc1967Utils::get_beacon_implementation(context, new_beacon)?;
278	
279	            AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
280	                context,
281	                beacon_implementation,
282	                data.as_ref(),
283	            )?;
284	        }
285	
286	        Ok(())
287	    }
288	}

291	    /// Reverts if `context.vm().msg_value()` is not
292	    /// [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]. It can be used to avoid
293	    /// `context.vm().msg_value()` stuck in the contract if an upgrade does not
294	    /// perform an initialization call.
295	    ///
296	    /// # Arguments
297	    ///
298	    /// * `context` - Read access to the contract's state.
299	    ///
300	    /// # Errors
301	    ///
302	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If `context.vm().msg_value()` is not
303	    ///   [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`].
304	    fn check_non_payable(
305	        context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>,
306	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
307	        if context.vm().msg_value().is_zero() {
308	            Ok(())
309	        } else {

311	        }
312	    }

385	        context: &mut T,
386	        new_beacon: Address,

1	//! An upgradeability mechanism designed for UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy
2	//! Standard) proxies as defined in [ERC-1822].
3	//!
4	//! [ERC-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
5	//!
6	//! The functions included here can perform an upgrade of an
7	//! [`Erc1967Proxy`], when this contract is set as the implementation
8	//! behind such a proxy.
9	//!
10	//! [`Erc1967Proxy`]: crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy

50	/// The version of the upgrade interface of the contract.
51	pub const UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION: &str = "5.0.0";
52	
53	/// The version number of the logic contract.
54	pub const VERSION_NUMBER: U32 = uint!(1_U32);
55	
56	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
57	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`]) execution
58	/// contexts.
59	///
60	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
61	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
62	///
63	/// Behavior:
64	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
65	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`]), `logic_flag == false` (i.e.,
66	///   the proxy’s storage does not contain this implementation-only flag).
67	///
68	/// Security notes:
69	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
70	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
71	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
72	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
73	        .finalize();
74	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
75	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
76	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
77	
78	    B256::new(slot)
79	};

82	mod sol {
83	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
84	
85	    sol! {
86	        /// The call is from an unauthorized context.
87	        #[derive(Debug)]
88	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
89	        error UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext();
90	
91	        /// The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.
92	        ///
93	        /// * `slot` - The unsupported UUID returned by the implementation.
94	        #[derive(Debug)]
95	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
96	        error UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID(bytes32 slot);
97	
98	        /// The contract is already initialized.
99	        #[derive(Debug)]
100	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
101	        error InvalidInitialization();
102	
103	        /// The version is not greater than the current version.
104	        ///

246	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
247	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
248	///
249	/// # Overview
250	///
251	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
252	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
253	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
254	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
255	///
256	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
257	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
258	/// upgrade flow.
259	///
260	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
261	///
262	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
263	///
264	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
265	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
266	/// slot:
267	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
268	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
269	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
270	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
271	///
272	/// ## Initialization Pattern
273	///
274	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
275	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
276	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
277	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
278	///   `only_proxy()`.
279	///
280	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
281	///
282	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
283	///
284	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
285	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
286	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
287	///    the proxy.
288	///
289	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
290	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
291	/// unauthorized upgrades.
292	///
293	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
294	///
295	/// ## Common Mistakes
296	///
297	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
298	///   number constant does not increase.
299	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
300	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
301	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
302	///
303	/// ## Security Considerations
304	///
305	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
306	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
307	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
308	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
309	///
310	/// # Usage
311	///
312	/// ```rust
313	/// extern crate alloc;
314	///
315	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
316	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
317	///
318	/// #[storage]
319	/// #[entrypoint]
320	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
321	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
322	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
323	///
324	///     // Your contract's state variables
325	///     value: StorageU256,
326	///     // ...
327	/// }
328	///
329	/// #[public]
330	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
331	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
332	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
333	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
334	///     }
335	///
336	///     // Your contract's functions
337	/// }
338	/// ```
339	///
340	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
341	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
342	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
343	#[storage]
344	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
345	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
346	    pub version: StorageU32,
347	}
348	
349	#[public]
350	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
351	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
352	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
353	    ///
354	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
355	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
356	    ///
357	    /// # Arguments
358	    ///
359	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
360	    #[constructor]
361	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
362	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
363	    }
364	
365	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
366	    /// (initializer-like).
367	    ///
368	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
369	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
370	    ///
371	    /// # Arguments
372	    ///
373	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
374	    ///
375	    /// # Errors
376	    ///
377	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
378	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
379	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
380	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
381	    ///
382	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
383	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
384	        if self.not_delegated().is_ok() {
385	            return Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(
386	                UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {},
387	            ));
388	        }
389	        if self.version.get() > VERSION_NUMBER {
390	            return Err(Error::InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion {
391	                current_version: self.version.get().to(),
392	            }));
393	        }
394	
395	        self.version.set(VERSION_NUMBER);
396	        Ok(())
397	    }
398	}

401	impl IUUPSUpgradeable for UUPSUpgradeable {
402	    fn upgrade_interface_version(&self) -> String {
403	        UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION.into()
404	    }
405	
406	    #[payable]
407	    fn upgrade_to_and_call(
408	        &mut self,
409	        new_implementation: Address,
410	        data: Bytes,
411	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
412	        self.only_proxy()?;
413	        self._upgrade_to_and_call_uups(new_implementation, &data)?;
414	
415	        let data_set_version =
416	            UUPSUpgradeableInterface::setVersionCall {}.abi_encode();
417	        AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
418	            self,
419	            new_implementation,
420	            &data_set_version,
421	        )?;
422	
423	        Ok(())
424	    }
425	}

427	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
428	    /// Get the logic contract version.
429	    ///
430	    /// # Arguments
431	    ///
432	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
433	    #[must_use]
434	    pub fn get_version(&self) -> U32 {
435	        VERSION_NUMBER
436	    }
437	
438	    /// Get the logic flag from the appropriate storage slot.
439	    ///
440	    /// # Arguments
441	    ///
442	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
443	    #[must_use]
444	    pub fn logic_flag(&self) -> StorageBool {
445	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageBool>(self, LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT)
446	    }
447	
448	    /// Return the value stored in the logic flag slot.
449	    ///
450	    /// # Arguments
451	    ///
452	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
453	    #[must_use]
454	    pub fn is_logic(&self) -> bool {
455	        self.logic_flag().get()
456	    }
457	
458	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
459	    ///
460	    /// Checks:
461	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`] (checked via
462	    ///    `!self.is_logic()`).
463	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
464	    ///    non-zero).
465	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
466	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
467	    ///
468	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
469	    ///
470	    /// # Security Implications
471	    ///
472	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
473	    /// implementation contract.
474	    ///
475	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
476	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
477	    ///
478	    /// # Edge Cases
479	    ///
480	    /// * Calls from [ERC-1167] minimal proxies are not guaranteed to pass this
481	    ///   check
482	    ///
483	    /// # Arguments
484	    ///
485	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
486	    ///
487	    /// # Errors
488	    ///
489	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If any of the above conditions is
490	    ///   not met
491	    ///
492	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
493	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
494	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
495	        if self.is_logic()
496	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation(self) == Address::ZERO
497	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
498	        {
499	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
500	        } else {
501	            Ok(())
502	        }
503	    }
504	
505	    /// Check that the execution is not being performed through a
506	    /// [`delegate_call`].
507	    ///
508	    /// This allows a function to be callable on the implementing contract
509	    /// but not through proxies.
510	    ///
511	    /// # Arguments
512	    ///
513	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
514	    ///
515	    /// # Errors
516	    ///
517	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the execution is performed via
518	    ///   [`delegate_call`].
519	    ///
520	    /// [`delegate_call`]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
521	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
522	        if self.is_logic() {
523	            Ok(())
524	        } else {
525	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
526	        }
527	    }
528	}

538	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
539	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
540	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
541	    ///
542	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
543	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
544	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
545	    ///
546	    /// # Arguments
547	    ///
548	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
549	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
550	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
551	    ///
552	    /// # Errors
553	    ///
554	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
555	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
556	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
557	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
558	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
559	    ///   not designed to handle it.
560	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
561	    ///   address.
562	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`] to the new
563	    ///   implementation fails.
564	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
565	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
566	    ///
567	    /// # Events
568	    ///
569	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the implementation
570	    ///   is upgraded.
571	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
572	        &mut self,
573	        new_implementation: Address,
574	        data: &Bytes,
575	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
576	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
577	            .proxiable_uuid(self.vm(), Call::new())
578	            .map_err(|_e| {
579	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
580	                    implementation: new_implementation,
581	                })
582	            })?;
583	
584	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
585	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
586	                .map_err(Error::from)
587	        } else {
588	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
589	                slot,
590	            }))
591	        }
592	    }
593	}

56	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
57	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`]) execution
58	/// contexts.
59	///
60	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
61	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
62	///
63	/// Behavior:
64	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
65	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`]), `logic_flag == false` (i.e.,
66	///   the proxy’s storage does not contain this implementation-only flag).
67	///
68	/// Security notes:
69	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
70	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
71	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
72	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
73	        .finalize();
74	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
75	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
76	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
77	
78	    B256::new(slot)
79	};

246	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
247	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
248	///
249	/// # Overview
250	///
251	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
252	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
253	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
254	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
255	///
256	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
257	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
258	/// upgrade flow.
259	///
260	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
261	///
262	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
263	///
264	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
265	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
266	/// slot:
267	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
268	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
269	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
270	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
271	///
272	/// ## Initialization Pattern
273	///
274	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
275	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
276	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
277	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
278	///   `only_proxy()`.
279	///
280	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
281	///
282	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
283	///
284	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
285	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
286	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
287	///    the proxy.
288	///
289	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
290	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
291	/// unauthorized upgrades.
292	///
293	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
294	///
295	/// ## Common Mistakes
296	///
297	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
298	///   number constant does not increase.
299	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
300	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
301	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
302	///
303	/// ## Security Considerations
304	///
305	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
306	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
307	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
308	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
309	///
310	/// # Usage
311	///
312	/// ```rust
313	/// extern crate alloc;
314	///
315	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
316	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
317	///
318	/// #[storage]
319	/// #[entrypoint]
320	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
321	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
322	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
323	///
324	///     // Your contract's state variables
325	///     value: StorageU256,
326	///     // ...
327	/// }
328	///
329	/// #[public]
330	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
331	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
332	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
333	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
334	///     }
335	///
336	///     // Your contract's functions
337	/// }
338	/// ```
339	///
340	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
341	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
342	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
343	#[storage]
344	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
345	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
346	    pub version: StorageU32,
347	}
348	
349	#[public]
350	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
351	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
352	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
353	    ///
354	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
355	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
356	    ///
357	    /// # Arguments
358	    ///
359	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
360	    #[constructor]
361	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
362	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
363	    }
364	
365	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
366	    /// (initializer-like).
367	    ///
368	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
369	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
370	    ///
371	    /// # Arguments
372	    ///
373	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
374	    ///
375	    /// # Errors
376	    ///
377	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
378	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
379	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
380	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
381	    ///
382	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
383	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {

458	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
459	    ///
460	    /// Checks:
461	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`] (checked via
462	    ///    `!self.is_logic()`).
463	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
464	    ///    non-zero).
465	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
466	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
467	    ///
468	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
469	    ///

471	    ///
472	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
473	    /// implementation contract.
474	    ///
475	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
476	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
477	    ///
478	    /// # Edge Cases
479	    ///

481	    ///   check

490	    ///   not met

492	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
493	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
494	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
495	        if self.is_logic()
496	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation(self) == Address::ZERO
497	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
498	        {
499	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))

519	    ///

521	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
522	        if self.is_logic() {

538	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
539	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
540	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
541	    ///
542	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
543	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
544	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
545	    ///
546	    /// # Arguments
547	    ///
548	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
549	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
550	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
551	    ///
552	    /// # Errors
553	    ///
554	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
555	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
556	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
557	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
558	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
559	    ///   not designed to handle it.
560	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
561	    ///   address.
562	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`] to the new
563	    ///   implementation fails.
564	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
565	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
566	    ///
567	    /// # Events
568	    ///
569	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the implementation
570	    ///   is upgraded.
571	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
572	        &mut self,
573	        new_implementation: Address,
574	        data: &Bytes,
575	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
576	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
577	            .proxiable_uuid(self.vm(), Call::new())
578	            .map_err(|_e| {
579	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
580	                    implementation: new_implementation,
581	                })
582	            })?;
583	
584	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
585	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
586	                .map_err(Error::from)
587	        } else {
588	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
589	                slot,
590	            }))
591	        }
592	    }
593	}

#![cfg_attr(not(any(test, feature = "export-abi")), no_main)]
#![allow(clippy::needless_pass_by_value)]
extern crate alloc;

use alloc::vec::Vec;

use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::{
    erc1967::{self, Erc1967Proxy},
    IProxy,
};
use stylus_sdk::{
    abi::Bytes, alloy_primitives::Address, prelude::*, ArbResult,
};

#[entrypoint]
#[storage]
struct Erc1967Example {
    erc1967: Erc1967Proxy,
}

#[public]
impl Erc1967Example {
    #[constructor]
    pub fn constructor(
        &mut self,
        implementation: Address,
        data: Bytes,
    ) -> Result<(), erc1967::utils::Error> {
        self.erc1967.constructor(implementation, &data)
    }

    fn implementation(&self) -> Result<Address, Vec<u8>> {
        self.erc1967.implementation()
    }

    #[payable]
    #[fallback]
    fn fallback(&mut self, calldata: &[u8]) -> ArbResult {
        unsafe { self.erc1967.do_fallback(calldata) }
    }
}
